comments.author: Andrew Dubber
comments.text: MTSR reviews double-blind (CFP: "following a double-blind peer review process"). Name, ORCID, email and affiliation come out of the review copy and go back in for the camera-ready (18 Oct). For the camera-ready, LNCS wants institution, city and country: "Industry Commons Foundation, Stockholm, Sweden". And a question: would you use your ICF address as the contact? It's an ICF paper, and the affiliation and the address should agree.

comments.author: Andrew Dubber
comments.text: Two things. (1) Both links identify you (the ppquadrat handle), so they come out of the anonymised copy: use an anonymised mirror (anonymous.4open.science) or "repository link withheld for review". (2) Footnote 3 is a dead link: the v10 zip returns 404. The only GitHub release is benchmark-v9 (5 Aug); benchmark/v10 is in the tree and the README calls it current. Cut the v10 release or point at the directory before the camera-ready.

comments.author: Andrew Dubber
comments.text: PROV-O is cited in Section 2 and then not used. Say how Table 1 relates to it: is the record serialised as PROV-O, or as your own JSONL schema with a PROV-O mapping (Entity, Activity, Agent) as future work? And state the concrete form of the published artefact (benchmark.jsonl, alternatives.jsonl, manifest.json per the README) and the licence (CC BY 4.0 benchmark, MIT software). Metadata reviewers ask for format and licence first.

comments.author: Andrew Dubber
comments.text: Out for the review copy (ICF, Matteo and Harsh by name, the grant number all identify you); back in for the camera-ready. Separately, and for us rather than the paper: we deferred the Zenodo deposit at your request because the repository carries the benchmark pairs, and the paper invites readers to download the same pairs from GitHub. I know that GitHub doesn’t automatically seed LLMs in the same way as Zenodo does (according to Harsh and Matteo) but still worth a conscious decision or Matteo's confirmation.
